paragraphs.title: The Famine and the Journey to Egypt

easy.question: What did Jacob see was available in Egypt?
answers: Grain, meaning food
An army
A new land
easy.explanation: Jacob saw that grain, or food, was available for purchase in Egypt.

easy.question: Whom did Jacob tell to go down to Egypt?
answers: Joseph
His sons
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Jacob told his sons, “Go down there and buy food for us.”

easy.question: How many of Joseph’s brothers went down to Egypt?
answers: Seven
Ten
Twelve
easy.explanation: The verse says that ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to Egypt.

medium.question: Why did Jacob send his sons to Egypt?
answers: To buy food during the famine
To visit Joseph
To fight Egypt
medium.explanation: There was famine in Canaan, while grain was available in Egypt, so Jacob sent them to buy food.

medium.question: In the phrase “go down there, and buy for us,” what does “buy” refer to?
answers: Breaking something into pieces
Purchasing grain or food
Fleeing the place
medium.explanation: The context shows that Jacob wanted his sons to obtain food in Egypt.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: The brothers went to Egypt, and then Jacob heard about the food
Jacob heard that food was available in Egypt, and then sent his sons there
Benjamin went to Egypt, and then the brothers joined him
medium.explanation: First Jacob heard that grain was available; then he sent his sons to Egypt.

challenge.question: Why did Jacob not send Benjamin with his brothers?
answers: He feared that harm might come to him
Benjamin was already in Egypt
Benjamin was not his brother
challenge.explanation: Jacob feared that mischief might befall Benjamin.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that ten brothers went to Egypt while Benjamin stayed behind?
answers: Benjamin was the firstborn
Jacob especially protected Benjamin
Benjamin did not know about the famine
challenge.explanation: Jacob feared for Benjamin’s safety and therefore protected him more carefully than the others.

challenge.question: Why does the passage say that the sons of Israel came “among those that came”?
answers: They were among many people who came to buy food
They hid inside a house
They arrived after everyone else
challenge.explanation: Jacob’s sons were among the many people who came to Egypt because of the famine.

questions.question: Why did Jacob not send Benjamin with his brothers?
answers: He feared that harm might come to him
Benjamin was already in Egypt
Benjamin was not his brother
questions.explanation: Jacob feared that mischief might befall Benjamin.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that ten brothers went to Egypt while Benjamin stayed behind?
answers: Benjamin was the firstborn
Jacob especially protected Benjamin
Benjamin did not know about the famine
questions.explanation: Jacob feared for Benjamin’s safety and therefore protected him more carefully than the others.

questions.question: Why does the passage say that the sons of Israel came “among those that came”?
answers: They were among many people who came to buy food
They hid inside a house
They arrived after everyone else
questions.explanation: Jacob’s sons were among the many people who came to Egypt because of the famine.

easy.question: Who was governor over the land?
answers: Joseph
One of his brothers
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Joseph was governor over the land.

easy.question: What did Joseph’s brothers do when they came to him?
answers: They spoke angrily to him
They bowed down with their faces to the ground
They ran away
easy.explanation: Joseph’s brothers bowed down before him with their faces to the earth.

easy.question: Whom did Joseph recognize when he saw them?
answers: Men from Canaan
Pharaoh’s officials
His brothers
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joseph saw his brothers and knew them.

medium.question: Why did Joseph’s brothers come to Egypt?
answers: To buy food
To visit Pharaoh
To look for work
medium.explanation: They said they had come from Canaan to buy food.

medium.question: In “he sold to all the people of the land,” what did Joseph do?
answers: He commanded the army
He sold or distributed food
He served as the king’s messenger
medium.explanation: Joseph supplied food to the people of the land.

medium.question: What order of events is described?
answers: Joseph spoke to them, they arrived, and then he saw them
They bought food, Joseph recognized them, and then they bowed
The brothers arrived and bowed, Joseph recognized them, and then he spoke to them
medium.explanation: They arrived and bowed first; Joseph recognized them and then spoke to them.

challenge.question: What does it mean that Joseph “made himself strange” to them even though he knew them?
answers: He pretended not to know them
He forgot who they were
He ordered them to leave Egypt
challenge.explanation: Joseph acted as though they were strangers, although he recognized them.

challenge.question: Why did Joseph ask his brothers, “Whence come ye?” even though he knew them?
answers: He did not hear their answer
He was questioning them and wanted to hear their story
He thought they were Egyptians
challenge.explanation: Joseph questioned them like a ruler examining men from another country.

challenge.question: What does “bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth” express?
answers: Joy at seeing him
A request that Joseph go with them
Deep honor and submission before Joseph
challenge.explanation: Bowing with the face to the ground showed honor and submission before a person in authority.

questions.question: What does it mean that Joseph “made himself strange” to them even though he knew them?
answers: He pretended not to know them
He forgot who they were
He ordered them to leave Egypt
questions.explanation: Joseph acted as though they were strangers, although he recognized them.

questions.question: Why did Joseph ask his brothers, “Whence come ye?” even though he knew them?
answers: He did not hear their answer
He was questioning them and wanted to hear their story
He thought they were Egyptians
questions.explanation: Joseph questioned them like a ruler examining men from another country.

questions.question: What does “bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth” express?
answers: Joy at seeing him
A request that Joseph go with them
Deep honor and submission before Joseph
questions.explanation: Bowing with the face to the ground showed honor and submission before a person in authority.

paragraphs.title: The Accusation of Spying and the Brothers’ Defense

easy.question: What did Joseph accuse his brothers of being?
answers: Spies
Merchants
Shepherds
easy.explanation: Joseph told them, “Ye are spies.”

easy.question: Why did the brothers say they had come to Egypt?
answers: To search for Joseph
To buy food
To visit Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The brothers said that they had come to buy food.

easy.question: How many brothers did they say they were?
answers: Ten
Eleven
Twelve
easy.explanation: They said, “Thy servants are twelve brethren.”

medium.question: Why did the brothers tell Joseph that they were sons of one man?
answers: To show that they were a family, not a group of spies
To ask him for work
To announce that they were soldiers
medium.explanation: They tried to prove that they were an honest family rather than spies.

medium.question: In the phrase “to see the nakedness of the land,” what does “nakedness” mean?
answers: The beauty of the land
Its weaknesses or exposed places
Its houses
medium.explanation: In the context of spying, the phrase refers to vulnerable or exposed places in the land.

medium.question: What detail did the brothers give about their family?
answers: They all lived in Egypt
One brother was missing, and their youngest brother was with their father
Their father was with them in Egypt
medium.explanation: They said that their youngest brother was with their father and that one brother was not present.

challenge.question: What caused Joseph to remember his dreams while speaking with his brothers?
answers: He saw them arrive together and bow before him
They told him their dreams
Pharaoh reminded him of them
challenge.explanation: Their arrival and bowing reminded Joseph of his dreams about his family bowing before him.

challenge.question: What striking contrast appears in the brothers’ words about themselves?
answers: They say they are poor but ask for gold
They say they are honest, but Joseph suspects them of being spies
They say they are Egyptians, but Joseph knows they are Canaanites
challenge.explanation: They claim to be honest men, while Joseph continues to accuse them of spying.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ mention of the missing brother?
answers: They are giving complete family information to persuade Joseph
They want to hide their father’s identity
They already know Joseph is the missing brother
challenge.explanation: They provide family details, including the absent brother, to support their claim that they are brothers, not spies.

questions.question: What caused Joseph to remember his dreams while speaking with his brothers?
answers: He saw them arrive together and bow before him
They told him their dreams
Pharaoh reminded him of them
questions.explanation: Their arrival and bowing reminded Joseph of his dreams about his family bowing before him.

questions.question: What striking contrast appears in the brothers’ words about themselves?
answers: They say they are poor but ask for gold
They say they are honest, but Joseph suspects them of being spies
They say they are Egyptians, but Joseph knows they are Canaanites
questions.explanation: They claim to be honest men, while Joseph continues to accuse them of spying.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the brothers’ mention of the missing brother?
answers: They are giving complete family information to persuade Joseph
They want to hide their father’s identity
They already know Joseph is the missing brother
questions.explanation: They provide family details, including the absent brother, to support their claim that they are brothers, not spies.

easy.question: What condition did Joseph set for testing the brothers?
answers: They had to bring their youngest brother
They had to return immediately to Canaan
They had to bring more money
easy.explanation: Joseph said they would be tested when they brought their youngest brother.

easy.question: How long did Joseph put the brothers in custody?
answers: One day
Three days
Seven days
easy.explanation: Joseph put them in custody for three days.

easy.question: What did Joseph say about himself on the third day?
answers: He was king of Egypt
He knew their father
He feared God
easy.explanation: On the third day Joseph said, “I fear God.”

medium.question: How did Joseph’s plan change after the three days of imprisonment?
answers: Only one brother would remain imprisoned, while the others would bring food home
All the brothers would stay in prison until Jacob came
Joseph would release them without testing their words
medium.explanation: Instead of keeping them all in custody, Joseph kept only one brother and sent the others for food.

medium.question: In “carry corn for the famine of your houses,” what does “corn” mean?
answers: Tools for dealing with famine
Food and supplies for the famine
A story about the famine
medium.explanation: Joseph sent them to bring food for their households during the famine.

medium.question: Why did Joseph require the brothers to bring their youngest brother?
answers: So he could study in Egypt
So he could help them buy food
So Joseph could test whether their story was true
medium.explanation: The younger brother’s arrival would show whether the brothers were telling the truth.

challenge.question: What was the purpose of Joseph’s oath, “By the life of Pharaoh”?
answers: To emphasize the seriousness of his oath and words
To say that Pharaoh was at home
To announce that the king had died
challenge.explanation: The expression is a solemn declaration that emphasizes the seriousness of Joseph’s demand.

challenge.question: What detail shows that Joseph eased his demand after testing the brothers?
answers: He required all of them to remain in prison
He kept only one brother in custody
He gave up requiring the youngest brother
challenge.explanation: At first all were to be held, but later Joseph kept only one brother in custody.

challenge.question: How are Joseph’s words, “I fear God,” connected to his proposal?
answers: They explain why he wants to act fairly rather than kill them
They prove that he does not believe them
They show that he intends to worship Egypt’s gods
challenge.explanation: Joseph presents fear of God as a reason to deal with them justly and mercifully while still testing them.

questions.question: What was the purpose of Joseph’s oath, “By the life of Pharaoh”?
answers: To emphasize the seriousness of his oath and words
To say that Pharaoh was at home
To announce that the king had died
questions.explanation: The expression is a solemn declaration that emphasizes the seriousness of Joseph’s demand.

questions.question: What detail shows that Joseph eased his demand after testing the brothers?
answers: He required all of them to remain in prison
He kept only one brother in custody
He gave up requiring the youngest brother
questions.explanation: At first all were to be held, but later Joseph kept only one brother in custody.

questions.question: How are Joseph’s words, “I fear God,” connected to his proposal?
answers: They explain why he wants to act fairly rather than kill them
They prove that he does not believe them
They show that he intends to worship Egypt’s gods
questions.explanation: Joseph presents fear of God as a reason to deal with them justly and mercifully while still testing them.

easy.question: Regarding whom did the brothers say they were guilty?
answers: Joseph
Simeon
Reuben
easy.explanation: They said, “We are guilty concerning our brother,” meaning Joseph.

easy.question: What had the brothers done when Joseph pleaded with them?
answers: They listened to him
They would not listen to him
They released him
easy.explanation: They admitted that they had seen Joseph’s anguish but had not listened to him.

easy.question: What did Joseph do after hearing his brothers’ words?
answers: He laughed
He left the place
He wept
easy.explanation: Joseph turned away and wept before returning to speak with them.

medium.question: Why did the brothers say that distress had come upon them?
answers: Because they had not listened to Joseph’s pleas
Because they had lost their money
Because Reuben was angry with them
medium.explanation: They connected their present trouble with their earlier sin against Joseph.

medium.question: In the phrase “he spake unto them by an interpreter,” what was the interpreter’s role?
answers: A judge between them
A translator between them
Their enemy
medium.explanation: The brothers did not realize Joseph understood them because they thought the interpreter alone translated their words.

medium.question: What did Joseph do before taking Simeon?
answers: He sent the brothers home
He punished Reuben
He turned away, wept, and then spoke with them again
medium.explanation: Joseph first turned away and wept, then returned to speak with them before taking Simeon.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Joseph’s weeping in private before returning to his brothers?
answers: Their words deeply moved him
He did not understand them
He was happy to punish them
challenge.explanation: Joseph’s hidden tears show that their words stirred strong emotions in him.

challenge.question: Why did the brothers not know that Joseph understood them?
answers: Joseph remained silent
There was an interpreter between them
They were speaking Egyptian
challenge.explanation: They thought the interpreter was the only person who understood their language.

challenge.question: What does Reuben mean by “his blood is required”?
answers: Joseph’s blood is being shed now
Joseph demands to see their blood
They must answer for what they did to Joseph
challenge.explanation: Reuben means that responsibility for harming Joseph has come back upon them.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Joseph’s weeping in private before returning to his brothers?
answers: Their words deeply moved him
He did not understand them
He was happy to punish them
questions.explanation: Joseph’s hidden tears show that their words stirred strong emotions in him.

questions.question: Why did the brothers not know that Joseph understood them?
answers: Joseph remained silent
There was an interpreter between them
They were speaking Egyptian
questions.explanation: They thought the interpreter was the only person who understood their language.

questions.question: What does Reuben mean by “his blood is required”?
answers: Joseph’s blood is being shed now
Joseph demands to see their blood
They must answer for what they did to Joseph
questions.explanation: Reuben means that responsibility for harming Joseph has come back upon them.

paragraphs.title: The Grain and the Returned Money

easy.question: What did Joseph command to be put in the brothers’ sacks?
answers: Grain, money, and provisions
Clothes and water
Gold and jewelry
easy.explanation: Joseph filled their sacks with grain, returned their money, and gave them provisions.

easy.question: What did the brothers carry their grain on?
answers: Their shoulders
Their donkeys
Carts
easy.explanation: The passage says that they loaded the grain onto their donkeys.

easy.question: What did one brother see when he opened his sack?
answers: His brother
More bread
His money at the mouth of the sack
easy.explanation: He saw that his money had been returned and was inside the opening of his sack.

medium.question: Why did one brother open his sack at the lodging place?
answers: To check his money
To give provender to his donkey
To take out grain to sell
medium.explanation: He opened the sack to feed his donkey and then noticed his money.

medium.question: In “to give his ass provender,” what does “provender” mean?
answers: Drinking water
A riding tool
Food for an animal
medium.explanation: Provender is food for a beast, such as a donkey.

medium.question: How did the brothers react after discovering that the money had been returned?
answers: They were afraid and asked what God had done to them
They rejoiced and returned to Egypt
They became angry with the donkeys
medium.explanation: Their hearts failed them, and they fearfully asked what God had done to them.

challenge.question: What shows that the brothers discovered the money only after leaving Egypt?
answers: They found it at the lodging place after traveling away
They received it beside Joseph
They found it before receiving the grain
challenge.explanation: They first left with the grain and only later discovered the money at the lodging place.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by “they were afraid, saying one to another”?
answers: Each turned to the others in fear and concern
Each said farewell to the others
Each returned alone to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The wording describes their mutual fear after finding the money.

challenge.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: A brother found the money, Joseph filled the sacks, and they left
Joseph ordered the sacks filled, the brothers left, and the money was found at the lodging place
The brothers returned to Egypt, received provisions, and fed the donkeys
challenge.explanation: Joseph first gave his instructions; the brothers left, and one later found his money.

questions.question: What shows that the brothers discovered the money only after leaving Egypt?
answers: They found it at the lodging place after traveling away
They received it beside Joseph
They found it before receiving the grain
questions.explanation: They first left with the grain and only later discovered the money at the lodging place.

questions.question: What is emphasized by “they were afraid, saying one to another”?
answers: Each turned to the others in fear and concern
Each said farewell to the others
Each returned alone to Egypt
questions.explanation: The wording describes their mutual fear after finding the money.

questions.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: A brother found the money, Joseph filled the sacks, and they left
Joseph ordered the sacks filled, the brothers left, and the money was found at the lodging place
The brothers returned to Egypt, received provisions, and fed the donkeys
questions.explanation: Joseph first gave his instructions; the brothers left, and one later found his money.

easy.question: To whom did the brothers return in Canaan?
answers: Jacob their father
The king of Egypt
The people of the land
easy.explanation: The brothers came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan.

easy.question: What did the brothers tell Jacob?
answers: Only that they had bought food
Everything that had happened to them
That they had stayed in Egypt
easy.explanation: They told Jacob all that had happened to them.

easy.question: How did the man, the lord of the land, speak to them?
answers: Kindly
Quietly
Roughly and harshly
easy.explanation: They said that the man spoke roughly to them.

medium.question: How were the man’s words connected to his accusation?
answers: He spoke harshly and accused them of being spies
He blessed them and sent them away peacefully
He asked them to remain in Canaan
medium.explanation: They reported that he spoke harshly and treated them as spies.

medium.question: In “he took us for spies of the country,” what are spies?
answers: People who sell food
People asking permission to enter
People who secretly examine a land
medium.explanation: The man accused them of secretly investigating the country.

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: The brothers came to Jacob, told him what happened, and described the man’s words
The man came to Jacob, and then the brothers left Canaan
Jacob accused the brothers, and then they spoke with the man
medium.explanation: The brothers first came to Jacob and then reported what the man had said.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the title “the lord of the land”?
answers: He was an ordinary market man
He had authority and ruled in the land
He was one of Jacob’s sons
challenge.explanation: The title presents the man as someone with power and authority in the land.

challenge.question: What does “all that befell unto them” emphasize?
answers: They hid the main events from Jacob
They reported only the man’s words
They gave Jacob a complete account of what happened
challenge.explanation: The word “all” indicates that they reported the whole experience.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the word “us” in “he took us for spies”?
answers: The man accused all the brothers together
He accused only Jacob
He accused only one brother
challenge.explanation: “Us” refers to the group of brothers, showing that the accusation applied to all of them.

questions.question: What can be understood from the title “the lord of the land”?
answers: He was an ordinary market man
He had authority and ruled in the land
He was one of Jacob’s sons
questions.explanation: The title presents the man as someone with power and authority in the land.

questions.question: What does “all that befell unto them” emphasize?
answers: They hid the main events from Jacob
They reported only the man’s words
They gave Jacob a complete account of what happened
questions.explanation: The word “all” indicates that they reported the whole experience.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the word “us” in “he took us for spies”?
answers: The man accused all the brothers together
He accused only Jacob
He accused only one brother
questions.explanation: “Us” refers to the group of brothers, showing that the accusation applied to all of them.

easy.question: What did the brothers say about themselves?
answers: They were honest men, not spies
They were kings in Canaan
They were looking for work in Egypt
easy.explanation: They said, “We are true men; we are no spies.”

easy.question: How many brothers did they say they were?
answers: Ten
Twelve
Fourteen
easy.explanation: They said, “We be twelve brethren.”

easy.question: Where was the youngest brother?
answers: In Egypt
On the way to Egypt
With his father in Canaan
easy.explanation: The youngest brother was with their father in Canaan.

medium.question: Why did the brothers add details about their number and family?
answers: To strengthen their claim that they were a family, not spies
To announce that they wanted to leave Canaan
To ask Joseph to become their brother
medium.explanation: The family details were meant to support their claim that they were not spies.

medium.question: In “We are true men,” what does “true” mean?
answers: Young
Honest and trustworthy
Strong and wealthy
medium.explanation: They were claiming to be honest and reliable men.

medium.question: What is the order of the brothers’ statements?
answers: They mention the youngest, then say they are brothers
They say they are spies, then deny it
They declare that they are honest, then describe their family
medium.explanation: They first call themselves honest and then give details about their twelve brothers and father.

challenge.question: What can be known with certainty from “one is not”?
answers: One brother is absent, but the verse does not say that he is dead
One brother is with Pharaoh
One brother was never part of the family
challenge.explanation: The phrase only says that one brother is absent; it does not explain what happened to him.

challenge.question: If there are twelve brothers, one is absent, and the youngest is with his father, how many are with the speakers?
answers: Nine
Ten
Eleven
challenge.explanation: Twelve minus the absent brother and the youngest brother leaves ten with the speakers.

challenge.question: What does “sons of our father” emphasize?
answers: All the brothers were born in the same city
All the brothers work together
They share a father and belong to the same family
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes their family connection through their father.

questions.question: What can be known with certainty from “one is not”?
answers: One brother is absent, but the verse does not say that he is dead
One brother is with Pharaoh
One brother was never part of the family
questions.explanation: The phrase only says that one brother is absent; it does not explain what happened to him.

questions.question: If there are twelve brothers, one is absent, and the youngest is with his father, how many are with the speakers?
answers: Nine
Ten
Eleven
questions.explanation: Twelve minus the absent brother and the youngest brother leaves ten with the speakers.

questions.question: What does “sons of our father” emphasize?
answers: All the brothers were born in the same city
All the brothers work together
They share a father and belong to the same family
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes their family connection through their father.

paragraphs.title: The Ruler’s Demand for Proof of Their Honesty

easy.question: Who told the brothers, “Hereby shall I know that ye are true men”?
answers: The man, the lord of the land
Jacob their father
The youngest brother
easy.explanation: The brothers reported that the ruler of the land had said this.

easy.question: Which brother were they commanded to bring to the man?
answers: The oldest brother
The youngest brother
The brother left in Egypt
easy.explanation: The man ordered them to bring their youngest brother.

easy.question: What would happen if they brought their youngest brother?
answers: They would return without food
The man would imprison them all
The man would give them their brother and allow them to trade in the land
easy.explanation: The man promised to return their brother and allow them to trade in the land.

medium.question: What did the brothers have to do to prove that they were not spies?
answers: Leave one brother with the man and bring their youngest brother
Return all the money to Egypt
Bring their entire family
medium.explanation: The man required one brother to remain while they brought their youngest brother.

medium.question: In “that ye are true men,” what does “true” mean?
answers: Rich
Truthful and honest
Fast
medium.explanation: The man wanted to know whether their words were truthful.

medium.question: Why did the man require them to bring their youngest brother?
answers: So he could be their leader
So they could teach him to trade
To test whether their story was true and they were not spies
medium.explanation: Bringing the youngest brother would support their claim that they were brothers, not spies.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the man saying both “ye are true men” and “ye are no spies”?
answers: He required practical proof that their claim was true
He already completely trusted them
He wanted to punish them for trading
challenge.explanation: The repeated ideas show that he was testing their honesty by requiring the youngest brother’s arrival.

challenge.question: What does “ye shall traffick in the land” mean in context?
answers: They would leave the land forever
They would be allowed to continue buying and selling there
They would rule the land instead of the man
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that they would be allowed to continue trading in the land.

challenge.question: Which detail in the man’s condition is especially important?
answers: All the brothers would remain in Egypt
The youngest would remain with the man while another brother returned
One brother would remain with the man, and the youngest would be brought to him
challenge.explanation: One brother was to stay behind while the others brought the youngest brother.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the man saying both “ye are true men” and “ye are no spies”?
answers: He required practical proof that their claim was true
He already completely trusted them
He wanted to punish them for trading
questions.explanation: The repeated ideas show that he was testing their honesty by requiring the youngest brother’s arrival.

questions.question: What does “ye shall traffick in the land” mean in context?
answers: They would leave the land forever
They would be allowed to continue buying and selling there
They would rule the land instead of the man
questions.explanation: The phrase means that they would be allowed to continue trading in the land.

questions.question: Which detail in the man’s condition is especially important?
answers: All the brothers would remain in Egypt
The youngest would remain with the man while another brother returned
One brother would remain with the man, and the youngest would be brought to him
questions.explanation: One brother was to stay behind while the others brought the youngest brother.

paragraphs.title: The Money Is Discovered and Fear Enters Jacob’s Household

easy.question: What did each brother find in his sack?
answers: Bread
A bundle of money
A garment
easy.explanation: Each brother found his bundle of money in his sack.

easy.question: Who said, “Me have ye bereaved of my children”?
answers: Joseph
Simeon
Jacob
easy.explanation: The verse identifies Jacob as the speaker.

easy.question: How did the brothers and their father react when they saw the money?
answers: They were afraid
They rejoiced
They laughed
easy.explanation: The passage says that they were afraid.

medium.question: Why did Jacob feel that all these troubles had come upon him?
answers: The household had run out of food
Joseph was gone, Simeon was gone, and Benjamin was now being taken
The brothers had lost their money
medium.explanation: Jacob listed Joseph’s absence, Simeon’s absence, and the possible loss of Benjamin.

medium.question: In “Me have ye bereaved of my children,” what does “bereaved” mean?
answers: You have made me happy
You have fed me
You have caused me to lose my sons
medium.explanation: Jacob meant that he had suffered the loss of his children.

medium.question: What happened before the brothers and their father became afraid?
answers: They emptied their sacks and found the money
Jacob sent them back to Egypt
Benjamin returned home
medium.explanation: They first emptied the sacks and found the bundles of money.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the plural expression “bundles of money”?
answers: Only one brother had money
Each brother found a bundle of money
The money was outside the sacks
challenge.explanation: The plural expression indicates that every brother found his own bundle of money.

challenge.question: What do Jacob’s words, “ye will take Benjamin away,” reveal about his attitude toward Benjamin?
answers: He did not know Benjamin
He was especially afraid of losing Benjamin too
He wanted to send Benjamin alone
challenge.explanation: Jacob includes Benjamin’s possible loss with the losses of Joseph and Simeon, showing his great fear.
